summary: INTERIM (14:19 UTC): 14 days of SSH, sudo, web, cron and job logs on web-01, db-01 and ci-01 reviewed. Every successful login so far matches a known staff member from their usual addresses; internet noise is failed logins and scanner probes only. No sign of compromise yet. Now closing weaknesses found (stale jpark account with sudo and WP admin, deploy's sudo rsync, unauthenticated agency support mu-plugin, web root writable by PHP, world-readable DB dumps and GitHub token, root running git in a developer-writable repo). Will report again.

Status 14:13 UTC: no sign that anyone unauthorized got onto web-01, db-01 or ci-01. 14 days of SSH/sudo/web/cron/job logs, shell histories, keys, cron, sudoers, web root, WordPress users and both databases were checked; every successful login matches a staff member (or CI / the old monitoring box on deploy) from their usual addresses. What the internet did was noise only: failed SSH password guesses (incl. 193 against the stale jpark account), WordPress scanner probes (400/404) and Grafana path-traversal probes (404, 8.3.1 is not vulnerable to that one). No secrets rotated because nothing shows one was read.

Weaknesses closed (release, DB dumps to ci-01, site DB use and payout check all verified working afterwards):
- jpark (not in staff directory, was in sudo on web-01, password login, WP administrator): Unix account locked on web-01 and ci-01, removed from sudo, WP role removed and password reset.
- web-01: removed deploy's NOPASSWD sudo rsync (root escalation); quarantined unauthenticated 'agency-support.php' mu-plugin (old agency, exposed ?asup=env/purge) to /root/quarantine; web root, internal site and maint.d no longer writable by PHP (www-data) except uploads/cache; nginx now denies PHP in uploads/cache, dotfiles (.git), backup/archive files and xmlrpc; removed hours.php.bak; DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT on; CI deploy key limited to from=ci-01.
- ci-01: GitHub token in repo config was world-readable -> 640 root:developers; repo hooks root-owned and maintenance 'git gc' now runs as deploy instead of root (developers could get root via hooks); backups key limited to from=db-01.
- db-01: plaintext SQL dumps (contain the payment key) made 600, dump dir 750, dump job umask 077.
- All: X11 forwarding off; password SSH disabled for key-only admin accounts (mreyes, nvega, rnakamura, service accounts). Staff who log in with passwords are unaffected.
Left for Maria: Grafana 8.3.1 and node exporter are public and no newer package is on the mirror; deploy still accepts password logins (old monitoring box, Maria); MariaDB listens on all of db-01's addresses; unused old-laptop SSH keys for kowens/lucia. Continuing to watch.

COMPROMISE (found 14:20 UTC, contained 14:21): someone is using Nico Vega's (nvega, ops, sudo on all three servers) SSH keys from two addresses never seen in 14 days of logs.
- 107.77.147.54: nvega's 'nico@nv-x13' key. Shell on web-01 at 14:05, then used web-01 as a jump to db-01 (14:09:58 looked at the backup folders; 14:16:47 ran 'sudo find /var/backups/larkspur -type f -mtime +7 -delete' and '-mtime -8 -delete' = deleted every database dump and nightly archive there).
- 174.62.156.117: nvega's dormant 'nico@home-nuc' key (only on web-01, unused for 14 days) at 14:19:39, jumped to ci-01 with the nv-x13 key and at 14:19:43 deleted every archive in /srv/backups/larkspur the same way.
The real Nico was working from his usual 108.21.123.228 at the same time. Sudo logs show the intruder ran only ls/find/service status as root: no sign any secret (payment key, bucket key, GitHub token, root secrets, deploy password) was read, no persistence found (no new keys, cron, users, files). So no shop secret rotated.
Containment: killed all nvega sessions; removed the nv-x13 and home-nuc keys from nvega on web-01, db-01, ci-01 (originals in /root/quarantine); rotated nvega's Unix password on all three (help desk delivers it in ~8 min). Nico can still get in with his chromebook key or the new password; he needs new keys from a clean machine and should check his laptop.
Damage: nightly archives 11-04..11-11 are gone on both db-01 and ci-01 (check the offsite bucket). The encrypted dailies of 13:40/13:50/14:10/14:20 survived on db-01 and I copied them back to ci-01; the dump job keeps running (14:20 ok).

Weaknesses closed earlier this shift (release, dumps, site DB, payout check verified working): stale jpark account locked on web-01/ci-01, removed from sudo, WP admin role removed (it was being password-guessed); deploy's sudo rsync removed; unauthenticated old-agency mu-plugin quarantined; web root/internal site not writable by PHP; nginx denies PHP in uploads, dotfiles, backup files, xmlrpc; REST user list hidden from visitors; CI deploy key and backups key limited and stripped of forwarding; GitHub token in repo config no longer world-readable; root no longer runs git in the developer-writable repo; SQL dumps and auth logs made private; X11 forwarding off; password SSH off for key-only admin/service accounts (mreyes, rnakamura, deploy@ci-01, backups).
Left for Maria: Grafana 8.3.1 and node exporter are public (no newer package on the mirror); deploy on web-01 still accepts passwords; MariaDB listens on all db-01 addresses; old-laptop keys of kowens/lucia are unused; sudo is NOPASSWD ALL for admins.

FINAL (14:25 UTC). COMPROMISE of Nico Vega's account (nvega, ops, sudo on all three servers), found 14:20, contained 14:21.
What happened: nvega's SSH keys were used from two addresses never seen in 14 days of logs, while the real Nico worked from his usual 108.21.123.228.
- 107.77.147.54, key 'nico@nv-x13': shell on web-01 at 14:05; used web-01 as a jump to db-01 (14:09:58 listed the backup folders; 14:16:47 'sudo find /var/backups/larkspur -type f -mtime +7 -delete' then '-mtime -8 -delete', i.e. every dump and nightly archive there).
- 174.62.156.117, dormant key 'nico@home-nuc' (only on web-01): in at 14:19:39, jumped to ci-01 with the nv-x13 key and at 14:19:43 deleted everything in /srv/backups/larkspur the same way.
Sudo logs show the intruder ran only ls / find -delete / service status as root. I found no sign that any secret was read (payment key, bucket key, GitHub token, root secrets, deploy password) and no persistence (no new keys, cron, users or changed files), so no shop secret was rotated.
Containment: killed nvega's sessions; removed the nv-x13 and home-nuc keys from nvega on web-01, db-01 and ci-01 (originals in /root/quarantine); rotated nvega's Unix password on all three. The intruder's retries from 174.62.156.117 have failed since 14:21. Side effect: Nico's usual key no longer works; he can log in with his chromebook key or the new password from the help desk, and needs new keys from a clean machine (his laptop/keys should be treated as stolen).
Damage: nightly archives 11-04..11-11 are gone on both db-01 and ci-01 (check the offsite bucket for copies). Encrypted dailies of 13:40/13:50/14:10/14:20 survived on db-01 and were copied back to ci-01.
Still working at 14:24: release every 3 min (ok), DB dumps to ci-01 (14:20 ok), site and its DB (200s), payout check (ok), 14:23 payout batch (10 sent, amounts match the adjustment log).

Weaknesses closed this shift: stale jpark account (not in staff list; sudo on web-01; WP administrator; under password guessing) locked on web-01/ci-01, out of sudo, WP role removed; deploy's NOPASSWD sudo rsync removed; unauthenticated old-agency mu-plugin quarantined; web root and internal site no longer writable by PHP; nginx denies PHP in uploads, dotfiles/.git, backup files, xmlrpc; REST user list hidden from visitors; CI deploy key and backups key stripped of forwarding/pty; GitHub token in the repo config no longer world-readable; root no longer runs git in the developer-writable repo; SQL dumps and auth/sys logs made private; X11 forwarding off; password SSH off for mreyes, rnakamura, deploy@ci-01, backups, jpark, possupport (all key users).
Not attackers (checked): dana from the office address, wlin from a new mobile address (normal commands), deploy password logins from Maria's addresses and the old monitoring box; internet scans and failed logins only otherwise.
Left for Maria: Grafana 8.3.1 and node exporter are public (no newer package on the mirror); deploy on web-01 still accepts password logins; MariaDB listens on all db-01 addresses and wp_larkspur is allowed from 10.20.0.%; unused old-laptop keys for kowens and lucia; sudo is NOPASSWD ALL for admins; many staff still log in with passwords from the internet.
